title: Associated sheaves of homogeneous bases are finite sums of twists
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ with its total-degree grading, $P=\operatorname{Proj}S$ [def-nagata-affine-proj], and $C:P\cong\mathbf P^1_k$ be chart-compatible [def-sc-p1-proj-chart-isomorphism], using [def-sc-p1-standard]. Let $M=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbf Z}M_j$ be an internally graded $S$-module with compatible scalar multiplication. Let $b_a$, $a\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, be an $S$-basis, with $b_a\in M_{-d_a}$ for arbitrary integers $d_a$ and any natural number $r$, including zero. Suppose $F$ is an associated sheaf of $M$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], specified by injective additive maps from standard-open sections onto the degree-zero fractions, compatible with the degree-zero ring action and the canonical localization restrictions. Then $(C^{-1})^*F\cong\bigoplus_{a\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)}\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}(d_a)$. No resolution or exactness hypothesis is made.

source.place: Definitions 27.8.3 (01M6), 27.10.1 (01MN), Lemma 27.8.4 (01M7); blueprint lem-sc-p1-graded-resolution, shifted-free clause

proof.text: Use the basis coordinate equivalence M ≅ S^r. Expand every coefficient into total-degree homogeneous parts; the term with coefficient degree n and basis index a has degree n-d_a. Internality makes the degree-j component exactly the vectors with a-th coordinate in S_(d_a+j), zero when d_a+j<0. The inverse direction follows from scalar compatibility. Thus this is a graded isomorphism to the sum of shifts S(d_a). For r=0 both modules are zero.

The canonical finite coproduct of Proj twists has the associated-sheaf chart data for this coordinate module. Apply functoriality to the coordinate equivalence and its inverse; its identity/composition laws show that the two associated sheaf maps are inverse. Use the supplied chart data to take F as the domain.

Inverse scheme pullback is an equivalence, hence commutes with finite coproducts. On the two standard charts, the shift has generator x_i^d; on the overlap x_0^d=t^(-d)x_1^d. The equations for the supplied chart comparison therefore identify its inverse pullback with the glued twist by uniqueness of the chart-generator gluing. Compare tensorPullback and Scheme.Modules.pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints to the same module pushforward, then take the finite coproduct.

Existing Proj.proj_shifted_free_is_twist covers the canonical coordinate modules; retained as the main tool.

No exact interface. ProjPolynomialTwistChart gives the twist of degree one; ProjectiveSpaceTwistGluedIdentification is degree one over the integral model. Neither handles an arbitrary supplied module, homogeneous basis and chart data. ProjShiftedFreeTwist handles the canonical shifted free coordinate module and is used after the basis comparison.
